title: Bounded exact-term Hom preserves quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on a small category $C$, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $P$ a cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules. Suppose $P^n=0$ outside a finite interval and that each functor $\mathcal Hom_R(P^n,-)$ sends short exact sequences to short exact sequences. For every quasi-isomorphism $f:M\to N$ of arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], the induced map $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,M)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,N)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08DM (cohomology-lemma-RHom-strictly-perfect), bounded Hom calculation; homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain) for finite-filtration induction

proof.text: Induct on a natural interval width d with P supported in [a,a+d]. For d=0 apply the single-degree Hom theorem at a. Internal Hom from zero is zero, so all-zero sources are included.

For a successor width, form the real Mathlib stupid tail U in degrees at least a+1. It is supported in [a+1,a+1+d]. Its terms are either zero or isomorphic to the corresponding P terms. Prove exactness for zero sources and transport short exactness along those isomorphisms. Apply the induction hypothesis to U. Apply the single-degree theorem to P^a placed in degree a, transporting the exact-term hypothesis along singleObjXSelf.

Use the natural short exact Hom sequences for the stupid tail. Transport the two outer quasi-isomorphisms through their arrow isomorphisms. Apply the proved upstream HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.quasiIso_τ₂ (WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.BicomplexColumns), whose long-exact-sequence proof uses the five lemma. Transport the middle quasi-isomorphism back through its arrow isomorphism.
For the original bounds a,b take d=(b-a).toNat. Then b is at most a+d, including b<a; the given bounds imply the interval hypothesis. Apply the proved finite induction.
